key_insight: Fully implicit Radau IIA time integration can be computationally competitive for Rayleigh–Bénard convection when paired with scalable multigrid preconditioners.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports efficient simulation of buoyancy-driven thermal flows while addressing incompressibility and coupled velocity–pressure–temperature dynamics.
method: High-order, L-stable Radau IIA integration of the incompressible Boussinesq equations.
Taylor–Hood and macroelement finite element discretizations in two and three dimensions.
Multigrid preconditioning of stage-coupled systems, with macroelement patches suited to Vanka relaxation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports nearly stage-independent Krylov iterations and mesh-robust convergence in 2D, 18–32% lower solve times for selected Radau configurations with incremental pressure correction, and favorable parallel scalability with Taylor–Hood elements in 3D.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on the integration configuration, discretization, and preconditioner; the reported speedups should not be assumed universal.
paper_title: Scalable Fully Implicit Runge-Kutta Solvers for Time-Dependent Rayleigh-Bénard Convection
